Rather than responding to dozens of comments and pm's, I will just answer your questions here. If you don't care please ignore and have a good day.

The HenryCorp and /v/pics situations were the impetus that helped me to understand a larger problem existed. When I originally decided to fight for these issues I wrongly assumed people would revolt once they learned what was happening. However in time it became clear to me that a large portion of the community (including the so-called "protect voat" people) actually supported strictly enforced rules (up to and including deletion of content with many upvoats) and "benevolent dictators" on defaults. To my great surprise people were unable or unwilling to understand that just because you happen to like the current regime doesn't mean you are free. They insisted that it was ok, even necessary, to have lots of rules (censorship) "for the greater good" of the community. They said it was ok because if things ever got out of hand the admins could step in if needed. They didn't seem to realize that they are being subjected to a kind of voluntary soft censorship where they are routinely and easily censored and manipulated. And they seemed almost entirely unwilling to take seriously, or even discuss, the issue of ccp abuse/farming/manipulation.

This was a hard pill to swallow. I had the misconception that Voat was supposed to be a bastion of freedom and that the community/admins would never tolerate censorship (at least not in defaults) or abuse of voating privileges. All the while it was happening right under my nose. When I realized my error I felt cheated, and stupid. However that was only half of the problem. I struggled with overwhelming disappointment as I realized the admins seemed unlikely to officially address these problems. I don't know if it comes down to a lack of time, or vision, or fear of making things worse, or something else. In a way I understand because they are unpaid volunteers with full time jobs and it must be really difficult to feed the monster they have created. I wouldn't be surprised if they regret it sometimes. I genuinely respect and appreciate what they have built for us and I have tried to be patient and supportive and to not expect too much from them, but it just kills me to see this happen because I feel this weird project called Voat has so much potential and is so important - real freedom is exceedingly rare in this world.

I have also met some truly amazing people through Voat. They have made my life richer and more interesting and have continually challenged my ideas and forced me to work hard to see and understand the world differently. I can honestly say I am not the same person I was a year ago and Voat is largely responsible for that (in a good way, I think). That is the reason I was willing to fight so hard and is also the reason I have found it difficult to just walk away. And so it is for that reason and a sense of respect that I wanted to explain my departure and say thanks to those who have helped me to pass the time and to learn and grow as a person. It's been fun. I will continue to hope that in time Voat can overcome its growing pains and become a truly free and open platform. And if that happens maybe I will give it another try some day.
